agenda_text:
City of Encinitas
Regular City Council Meeting - 6:00 p.m.
AGENDA
WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 21, 2019 -
6:00
p.m.
City of Encinitas - City Council Chambers
505 S. Vulcan Avenue
Encinitas, California 92024
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council.
1.
CALL TO ORDER
2.
ROLL CALL
3.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
4.
SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS AND PROCLAMATIONS
4A.
Presentation by Fire Chief Stein regarding wildfire preparedness.
4B.
Presentation by Executive Officer Keene Simonds regarding the purpose and responsibilities of San Diego Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) and presentation of commendation to Mayor Blakespear for her service to LAFCO
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. Time donations are not permitted during Oral Communications. Please submit a “WHITE” speaker slip to the City Clerk. If needed, Oral Communication items will be referred to the City Manager either for resolution by administrative action or placement on a future agenda.
6.
REPORT FROM CLOSED SESSION (IF HELD)
7.
CHANGES TO THE AGENDA Announcements of administrative changes to the agenda, in compliance with the Brown Act.
The title of ordinances listed on this agenda are deemed to have been read and further reading waived.
8.
CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a “PINK” speaker slip to the City Clerk. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Council Member or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.
If a public hearing item is part of the consent calendar, the public hearing shall be deemed held if the item is not removed from the consent calendar for discussion and possible action.
8A.
Approval of the Minutes of the July 10, 2019 Special Meeting-Closed Session and the July 10, 2019 Regular Meeting. Contact Person: City Clerk Hollywood
Approve the Minutes.
2019-08-21 Item 08A Minutes
8B.
Approval of the Warrants List. Contact Person: Finance Manager Lundgren
Approve the Warrants.
2019-08-21 Item 08B Warrants
8C.
Designation of a voting delegate and voting delegate-alternate for the League of California Cities (LCC) Annual Conference, October 16-18, 2019. Contact Person: Executive Assistant to Mayor and City Council Clisby
City Council adopts Resolution 2019-75 designating Council Member Mosca to represent the City of Encinitas as a voting delegate and Council Member Hinze as voting delegate-alternate at the LCC Annual Conference to be held October 16-18, 2019, in Long Beach, California.
2019-08-21 Item 08C LCC Voting Delegate
8D.
Resolution Approving the Application for Prop 68 Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program Grant Funds. Contact Person: Park Operations Manager Saul
1) Approve a Resolution authorizing an application for grant funds from the Prop 68 Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program Grant Funds; and 2) Authorize the City Manager or City Manager’s Designee to enter into an agreement with the State Department of Parks and Recreation, in conjunction with the City Attorney, subject to current City Council budget appropriations.
2019-08-21 Item 08D Prop 68 Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program Grant Funds
8E.
Purchase of nine (9) cardiac monitors, two (2) cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) devices, and a five (5) year service agreement in the amount of $341,242 from Zoll Medical Corporation and approve trade-in of existing cardiac monitors; and off-cycle budget appropriation for the Fiscal Year 2019-20 Operating Budget for County Service Area 17 (CSA-17) Fund 230. Contact Person: Deputy Fire Chief Ford
1) Authorize the Encinitas Fire Department to utilize the Request for Proposal (RFP) approved by the County of Los Angeles awarding Zoll Medical Corporation the contract to provide for the purchase and warranty of cardiac monitors/defibrillators, accessories/supplies, and upgrades; 2) Authorize the Fire Chief to enter into an Agreement with Zoll Medical Corporation for the purchase of nine (9) cardiac monitors, two (2) cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) devices, a five (5) year service agreement, and approve trade-in of the eight (8) existing cardiac monitors in the amount of $341,242; and 3) Adopt Resolution No. 2019-62 approving an off-cycle budget appropriation for the Fiscal Year 2019-20 Operating Budget for the County Service Area 17 (CSA-17) Fund 230.
2019-08-21 Item 08E Budget Adjustment to CSA-17 Fund and Service Agreement with Zoll Medical Corporation
8F.
Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Encinitas and the Community Resource Center to provide free bread and pastry donations. Contact Person: Center Manager Goodsell
Approve and authorize the City Manager, in coordination with the City Attorney, to execute an ongoing Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the City of Encinitas and the Community Resource Center (CRC) to provide free bread and pastry donations from Vons to senior citizens at the Encinitas Community and Senior Center via the Fresh Rescue Program.
2019-08-21 Item 08F MOU Between the City of Encinitas and the Community Resource Center to Provide Free Bread and Pastry Donations.
8G.
Contract Amendment #3 for Infrastructure Engineering Corporation (IEC) to provide additional design and permitting services for the Olivenhain Trunk Sewer Project (CC04J). Contact Person: Engineer II Widelski
Authorize the City Manager, or designee, in coordination with the City Attorney, to execute a contract amendment and extensions, with Infrastructure Engineering Corporation (IEC) in the amount of $64,160 plus 15 percent contingency for a total contract amendment amount not to exceed $73,784 and a total contract cost not to exceed $927,461 to perform design and permitting services for the Olivenhain Trunk Sewer Project.
2019-08-21 Item 08G Olivenhain Trunk Sewer Improvements - Amendment #3 IEC Contract
8H.
Second Reading and Adoption of City Council Ordinance No. 2019-08, to adopt the modification suggested by the California Coastal Commission to City Council Ordinance No. 2019-04, which amended three Specific Plans, Municipal and Zoning Codes, and the local Coastal Program (LCP) to clarify provisions to implement the new General Plan Land Use designation and development standards. Contact Person: Principal Planner Gates
Adopt City Council Ordinance No. 2019-08, titled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, Adopting the Modification Suggested by the California Coastal Commission to City Council No. 2019-04, Amending the North 101 Corridor Specific Plan.”
2019-08-21 Item 08H Housing Element Coastal Commission Modification - Adoption of Ordinance
8I.
Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinance 2019-06, an Ordinance of the City of Encinitas, California, adding Encinitas Municipal Code Chapter 11.28 – Leaf Blower Ordinance. Contact Person: Environmental Programs Manager Steenblock
Adopt Ordinance 2019-06, titled “An Ordinance of the City of Encinitas, California, Adding Encinitas Municipal Code Chapter 11.28 – Leaf Blower Ordinance.”
2019-08-21 Item 08I Leaf Blower Ordinance - Adoption of Ordinance
8J.
Fourth Amendment to the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System San Diego Regional Stormwater Copermittees Memorandum of Understanding. Contact Person: Environmental Programs Manager Steenblock
Adopt Resolution 2019-65, approving the Fourth Amendment to the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System San Diego Regional Stormwater Copermittees Memorandum of Understanding, and authorize the City Manager to execute the Agreement.
2019-08-21 Item 08J 4th Amendment to Stormwater MOU
8K.
Notice of Completion for the Chesterfield Drive Quiet Zone Implementation Project (CS17F). Contact Person: City Engineer Wimmer
1) Accept the public improvements as complete; 2) Authorize release of the performance bond and initiate the warranty bond; and 3) Authorize filing of a Notice of Completion
2019-08-21 Item 08K NOC- Chesterfield Quiet Zone
8L.
Report on Emergency Repairs to Highway 101 Bridge over the San Elijo Lagoon (CX20A) and Ratify Budget Amendment to Fund Repairs. Contact Person: City Engineer Wimmer
Adopt Resolution No. 2019-69, entitled “A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas Ratifying the Amendment of the Fiscal Year 2019-20 Budget.”
2019-08-21 Item 08L Hwy 101 Bridge Emergency Repairs
8M.
Approval of a five-year Agreement between the County of San Diego and the City of Encinitas for California Identification System Remote Access Network (Cal-ID) and direct the City Manager to execute the agreement. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Approve a five-year Agreement with the County of San Diego for the Regional California Identification Remote Access Network (Cal-ID) and direct the City Manager to execute the agreement.
2019-08-21 Item 08M Cal-ID Agreement Report
8N.
Acceptance of the Coastal Rail Trail – Chesterfield Drive to Santa Fe Drive Segment. Contact Person: City Engineer Wimmer
Adopt Resolution No. 2019-68, entitled “A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas Accepting the Coastal Rail Trail – Chesterfield Drive to Santa Fe Drive Segment Project from the San Diego Associations of Governments.”
2019-08-21 Item 08N Acceptance of the Coastal Rail Trail
8O.
Capital Project and Grants Update – Capital Improvement Program and Traffic Engineering Divisions. Contact Person: City Engineer Wimmer
Receive the report on the status of Capital Improvement and Traffic Engineering projects and grants.
2019-08-21 Item 08O Mobility and Grant Report
8P.
Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with SANDAG for the El Portal Pedestrian and Bicycle Undercrossing Project (CS16F). Contact Person: City Engineer Wimmer
1) Authorize the City Manager, in consultation with the City Attorney, to execute the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with San Diego Association of Governments (SANDAG) for construction management of the El Portal Pedestrian and Bicycle Undercrossing project ; and 2) Direct staff to wire $500,000 to SANDAG upon execution of this MOU.
2019-08-21 Item 08P El Portal SANDAG MOU Report
8Q.
Legislative position letter in support of Senate Bill 2012 (Feinstein). Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Ratify the League of California Cities position letter in support of Senate Bill 2012.
2019-08-21 Item 08Q Legislative Support Letter Senate Bill 2012
8R.
Proposed personnel changes to the San Dieguito Water District and a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2019-20 Adopted Budget. Contact Person: Public Works Director Quiram
1) Change the title of General Manager to Assistant Director of Public Works/Assistant General Manager, upgrade Superintendent to Water Operations Manager and upgrade one Utility Maintenance Specialist to a Utility and Maintenance Supervisor I, as well as approve the related salary adjustments (including addition of Salary Step 10 to Grade 65 and correcting the prior omission of Finance Manager position) that accompany each change; 2) Approve the reorganization of transferring Wastewater Collections under the supervision of the newly created Assistant Director of Public Works/Assistant General Manager of a new Utilities Division of Public Works; 3) Adopt Resolution 2019-70 titled "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas Approving personnel changes to the Department of Public Works Pay Range Table and Position Titles" which amends the pay scales for the reclassified positions; and 4) Adopt Resolution 2019-61 titled "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas Amending the Fiscal Year 2019-20 Adopted Budget."
2019-08-21 Item 08R City Public Works Reorganization
8S.
Legislative position letter in support of SB 54/ AB 1080 (Allen/Gonzalez). Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Approve the position letter in support of SB54/AB 1080.
2019-08-21 Item 08S Legislative Support Letter SB 54 AB 1080
8T.
Legislative position letter in support of AB 1017 (Boerner Horvath). Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Approve the position letter in support of AB 1017.
2019-08-21 Item 08T Legislative Support Letter AB 1017
8U.
Legislative position letter for SB 266 (Leyva), Public Employees' Retirement System: Disallowed Compensation: Benefit Adjustments: Notice of Opposition. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Approve the position letter in support of SB 266 (Leyva).
2019-08-21 Item 08U Legislative Support Letter SB 266
9.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR Staff reports will be given only if requested by the person who pulled the item.
10.
ACTION ITEMS
PROCEDURES FOR PUBLIC HEARINGS ON APPEALS (ITEM 10A): New information such as documents, exhibits, letters, photos, charts, diagrams, videos, etc., WILL NOT be considered by the City Council if presented at this meeting. All material must have been submitted to the City Clerk no less than 7 calendar days prior to this hearing.

Public Hearing to consider a timely-filed appeal of the Planning Commission’s approval of the Miano Duplex Addition for the renovation of an existing duplex with a second-floor addition and use of a temporary construction trailer. CASE NUMBER: 18-169 DR/CDP; APPLICANT: Donna Miano; APPELLANT: Ken and Kristine Price; LOCATION: 404 and 406 Fourth Street (APN 258-074-01). Contact Person: Associate Planner Dichoso
Deny the appeal, uphold the approval of the Planning Commission decision and adopt draft City Council Resolution No. 2019-46.

10B.
Community Choice Energy Governance Analysis Report and CCE Formation. Contact Person: CAP Program Administrator Najera
1) Receive the Community Choice Energy (CCE) Governance Analysis Report ("EES Report") completed for the Cities of Encinitas, Del Mar, and Carlsbad; 2) Select the preferred CCE formation option (listed in order based on EES Report results): a. Partner Joint Powers Authority (JPA) - Cities of Encinitas, Del Mar, and Carlsbad; b. Solana Energy Alliance JPA - in partnership with Solana Energy Alliance (SEA); c. City of San Diego JPA - in partnership with City of San Diego; d. Enterprise CCE - City of Encinitas only; 3) Direct staff to prepare CCE formation documents, including CCE enabling ordinance and negotiated JPA agreement, as applicable, and return to Council for approval in time to submit an Implementation Plan to the California Public Utilities Commission by December 31, 2019 and launch the CCE in 2021; and 4) If the Partner JPA option is selected, direct staff to issue a Request for Proposals for contract services to prepare a CCE Implementation Plan for the Partners.
2019-08-21 Item 10B CCE Governance Analysis
2019-08-21 Item 10B CCE Governance Analysis - Supplemental Agenda Report (posted 8-21-2019)
10C.
Report Regarding the Federal Communications Commission's (FCC) Regulation of Small Cell Wireless Communication Facilities; and, Consideration and Possible Adoption of an Urgency Ordinance and Resolution to Establish Local Regulatory Framework for the Same. Contact Person: City Planner Sapau
1) Receive the report and presentation by staff and Telecom Law Firm, City Wireless Facilities Special Legal Counsel; 2) Adopt Ordinance No. 2019-12 (Attachment CC-1) on an urgency basis entitled "An Urgency Ordinance of the City of Encinitas, California, amending Encinitas Municipal Code Chapter 9.70 for the regulation of small wireless facilities and other infrastructure deployments in the public rights-of-way" that authorizes the City Council to regulate small wireless facilities and other infrastructure deployments in the public rights-of-way by a City Council policy adopted by resolution; 3) Adopt Resolution No. 2019-66 (Attachment CC-2) implementing new City Council Policy for the regulation of small wireless facilities and other infrastructure deployments in the public rights-of-way; and 4) Adopt Resolution No. 2019-67 (Attachment CC-3) adopting the Right-of-Way Administrative Design Review Permit and associated fee requirements for processing of small wireless facilities and other infrastructure deployments in the public rights-of-way.
2019-08-21 Item 10C Small Cell Wireless Facilities
10D.
Proposed changes to the e-mail retention policy. Contact Person: IT Manager Flynn
Authorize the revision of Administrative Policy G005 Section 5 E-MAIL to increase retention of e-mails from 30 days to two years and allow staff to save e-mails electronically rather than as hardcopy.
2019-08-21 Item 10D Proposed E-mail Retention Policy Revisions

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
